$comment: A node telling the platform what it can run, contract 1.11.0 (ADR 0029). Every field here is the machine's report about itself, and none of it is settable through the API — the same posture node.register already takes for image_upload and the codex sandbox flag (ADR 0023 D3). Note what is absent: there is no `enabled`. Whether a runner may take work is an administrator's decision, and letting a re-registration carry it would mean a daemon restart silently re-enabling something that was switched off.

runner_id.$comment: Present on re-registration only; the platform keys on node_id regardless, because a node holds exactly one runner row (ADR 0029 sec 1).

runtimes.$comment: Only the runtimes this node found to be *runner capable* — installed AND exposing both a non-interactive flag and a machine-readable event stream. A node whose CLI is too old reports an empty array and registers successfully: a failed registration reads as 'the machine is broken', while an empty set plus a reason on the Agents page reads as what it is (ADR 0029 sec 7).

labels.$comment: Displayed and **never compared** in V2.2. Label matching is a later feature; the field is carried now because the daemon already knows them, and dropping the value would make the console lie about what the node said.

max_concurrent.$comment: Runs executing at once. Lower bound 0 is legal and means 'registered but taking nothing', which is a useful state during maintenance.

max_waiting.$comment: A second limit, because a run in waiting_for_input holds no process and must not occupy execution capacity (ADR 0029 sec 5). Without it, three runs waiting on a human would take a node offline for work.

dedicated.$comment: **A report, never a setting.** Derived by the daemon from `len(workspace.allowed_roots) == 0`; Central stores it and displays it without checking it — the same requested/actual separation ADR 0023 D3 established for the codex sandbox flag. It matters because the platform has NO technical isolation between a run and the node's allowed roots (ADR 0031 sec 6): on a node with none, 'the run cannot read one' is vacuously true, and this field is what makes mixed use a visible choice instead of an unnoticed fact.
